NONE: › written abbreviation for adjective
形容詞（adjective的縮寫）
C2 very near, next to, or touching
鄰近的；毗連的

example: They work in adjacent buildings.
他們在相鄰的兩座樓裡工作。
They lived in a house adjacent to the railway.
他們家住在鐵路旁邊。

NONE: › one of the two angles on either side of a straight line that divides a larger angle into two
鄰角（由角分線將一個大角分成的相鄰兩個小角中的一個）
A2 a word that describes a noun or pronoun
形容詞

example: "Big", "boring", "purple", and "obvious" are all adjectives.
「大的」、「無聊的」、「紫色的」以及「明顯的」這些詞都是形容詞。

NONE: › to be very near, next to, or touching
緊挨；鄰接；貼近；毗連

example: The stables adjoin the west wing of the house.
馬廐緊挨著房子的西廂。
It's at this point that these three neighbourhoods adjoin.
這兒正是這三個街區的交界點。

NONE: › near, next to, or touching
鄰近的；毗鄰的

example: We asked for adjoining rooms.
我們要了相鄰的房間。

NONE: › to have a pause or rest during a formal meeting or trial
（使）休會；（使）休庭

example: The meeting was adjourned until Tuesday.
會議延期至星期二。
Shall we adjourn for lunch?
我們暫停先去吃午餐好嗎？

NONE: › to finish doing something and go somewhere, usually for a drink and some food
（通常指為享用飲食）到別處

example: Shall we adjourn to the sitting room for coffee?
我們到客廳喝杯咖啡好嗎？

NONE: › to announce a decision or consider something, especially officially
（尤指正式地）判決，宣判，裁決；認為

example: [ + to infinitive ] Half an hour into the game Paterson was adjudged to have fouled Jackson and was sent off.
比賽進行到半小時時，派特森被判對傑克遜犯規而被罰離場。
[ + noun/adj ] He was adjudged bankrupt by the court.
他被法庭宣判破產。
Fairbanks was adjudged the winner.
費爾班克斯被判定獲勝。

NONE: › to act as judge in a competition or argument, or to make a formal decision about something
擔任裁判；判決，裁定，裁決

example: He was asked to adjudicate on the dispute.
人們請他來對這場爭端作出裁定。
He was called in to adjudicate a local land dispute.
他被請來裁決一樁當地的土地糾紛。
[ + two objects ] The game was adjudicated a win for Black.
布萊克被裁定贏得比賽。

NONE: › a person or group that makes an official decision about something, especially about who is right in a disagreement
仲裁人；仲裁機構

example: She acted as adjudicator in the dispute.
她擔任了這場爭端的裁定人。

C: › formal something added or connected to a larger or more important thing
› specialized language In grammar, an adjunct is an adverb or phrase that gives extra information in a sentence.
修飾成分（文法中指在句子中提供附加資料的副詞或者副詞片語）

example: I hoped I would find the computer course a useful adjunct to my other studies.
我希望上了這門電腦課程後，會使其他科目的學習如虎添翼。

NONE: › to ask or order someone to do something
要求；命令；囑咐

example: The judge adjured him to answer truthfully.
法官要求他如實回答。

T: B2 [ T ] to change something slightly, especially to make it more correct, effective, or suitable
（尤指為了使某物更正確、有效或合適而）調整，調節
› [ T ] to arrange your clothing to make yourself look tidy

I: B2 [ I ] to become more familiar with a new situation

example: If the chair is too high you can adjust it to suit you.
如果椅子太高了，你可以把它調到適合你的高度。
As a teacher you have to adjust your methods to suit the needs of slower children.
作為一名老師，你必須調整教學方法來適應那些學得較慢的孩子的需要。
She adjusted her skirt, took a deep breath, and walked into the room.
她整理了一下裙子，深吸一口氣，走進了房間。
I can't adjust to living on my own.
我不習慣獨自生活。
Her eyes slowly adjusted to the dark.
她的眼睛慢慢適應了黑暗。
The lifestyle is so very different - it takes a while to adjust.
生活方式差別太大了，要過一段時間才能適應。

NONE: › able to be changed to suit particular needs
可調整的；可調節的

example: The height of the steering wheel is adjustable.
方向盤的高度可以調節。
Is the strap on this helmet adjustable?
這頂頭盔的扣帶可以調節嗎？

C or U: › the ability to become more familiar with a new situation

example: She made a few minor adjustments to the focus of her camera.
她稍微調了調照相機的焦距。
He has so far failed to make the adjustment from school to work.
他到現在還沒有適應從學生生活到工作的變化。

NONE: › a condition in which someone feels sad and hopeless as a result of a stressful event
適應障礙（一種情緒障礙，由於壓力事件而產生憂鬱、絕望等情緒）

example: Many of the symptoms in an adjustment disorder overlap with those of a diagnosis of major depression.
適應障礙的許多症狀跟重度憂鬱症相似。

NONE: › a military officer who does office work and who is responsible for rules and punishment among the lower ranks
（軍隊的）副官；人事行政參謀
